ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Represent an incomplete execution history as a set of possible histories, preserving both compliant and violating explanations until authoritative evidence distinguishes them. Possible compliance is not verified compliance. Possible violation is not a proven violation. Missing evidence must never be silently converted into a successful commit, a failed commit, or a definite fault.
ai_view.specification: Extend the in-build revocation-linearization spec (naya5/revocation-linearization) with RFD-AMB-1: the three-conclusion model (SAFETY_ESTABLISHED_IN_SCOPE / VIOLATION_ESTABLISHED / AMBIGUOUS_BOTH_POSSIBLE / INSUFFICIENT_MODEL_OR_OBSERVABILITY) with the quantifier semantics over H(O), the nonempty-completion-set check, and INCONSISTENT_OBSERVATIONS_OR_MODEL instead of vacuous PASS/FAIL; the partial-order history representation (operation_id, invocation/response/commit/effect evidence, outcome_set with UNRESOLVED, ordering_constraints, coverage_state, environment assumptions) — a missing receipt yields an unresolved operation, never a fabricated commit or abort; the MayViolate/MustViolate semantics with the invalid No/Yes row flagged; evidence-bound ambiguity records (RFD-AMB-1 schema: known_events, unresolved_operations, possible_histories with legal and violating witnesses, may/must_violate, next_discriminating_check, completion_coverage distinguishing exhaustive from bounded search); the twin-worlds acceptance experiment (identical observations for World L and World V; engine must return AMBIGUOUS_BOTH_POSSIBLE for both — D(Observe(h1))=D(Observe(h2)); then the staged evidence-revelation test 2A/2B updating in either direction without prejudgment); ten adversarial controls A1–A10 (missing receipts, timeouts, added receipts in both directions, untrusted logs, clock skew, inconsistent observations, independent-claim preservation); evidence-monotonic refinement (O1⊆O2 ⇒ H(O2)⊆H(O1); contradictions flagged, not silently discarded; disqualified observations or model revisions are governed expansions); safe operational behavior during ambiguity (his activity table: historical inspection permitted, certification withheld, blind retries forbidden without reconciliation, LEARN promotion held, Smart Notes preserve both worlds); two-layer model checking (Layer A concrete executions, Layer B observable histories; Observe(H_L)=Observe(H_V)=O; the diagnosis engine operates only on O — detecting answer-key leakage); the NayaPOWER alignment note (propagation.py's undetermined regions, authority.py's undetermined-evidence gating, fairness_verify.py's trace harness as building blocks, not proof of the protocol). The Ambiguous History Integrity Law. Highest-value next experiment: RFD-AMB-001 (two controlled executions, identical observations, withheld effect evidence; verifier establishes both worlds compatible, worker returns AMBIGUOUS_BOTH_POSSIBLE, staged release narrows correctly, removal restores ambiguity, unaffected claims preserved, cold successor reconstructs uncertainty).

decisions: Shawn's explicit framework, main chat, 2026-10-10. His word IS the verification (Verification Law).
Folded as the AMBIGUITY-QUALIFICATION extension of the in-build revocation-linearization layer — RFD-POS-1 says 'I don't know'; RFD-AMB-1 makes 'I don't know' rigorous.
intelligence.essence: Ambiguous History Integrity Law: when incomplete observations admit both legal and violating executions, NayaNET must preserve both possibilities, withhold definitive certification or blame, identify the missing discriminating evidence, and prohibit dependent consequential use of the unresolved proof. New admissible evidence may narrow the possibilities, but missing evidence may never be silently treated as proof of success, failure, or nonexecution. The defining behavior: 'We know the request was sent and revocation committed. We cannot yet establish whether the effect committed before or after revocation. Both outcomes remain possible. Here is the independent evidence needed to distinguish them, and here is what we can safely continue doing in the meantime.' This is an information limitation, not an intelligence limitation — and an autonomous system must be able to act on the fact that a proof is missing without claiming the feared violation occurred. The twin-worlds test is the honesty mechanism: indistinguishable observations must never produce different diagnoses, or the engine is leaking the answer key.
intelligence.falsifier: Missing evidence silently converted into a commit, abort, or fault; a speculative violating completion presented as a proven violation; a bounded search's legal-only results presented as universal safety; timestamps or worker labels manufacturing ordering edges; both 'all histories safe' and 'all histories violate' claimed on an empty completion set; inconsistent observations producing a vacuous PASS; a blind retry of an uncertain external action; a LEARN promotion asserting a root cause without causal evidence; a cold successor inheriting the conclusion without the uncertainty.

human_view.meaning: When the evidence can't answer the question, the honest answer is 'we don't know' — and 'we don't know' has rules. Picture two identical crime scenes: a request went out, a revocation committed, and the receipt showing what happened next is missing. In one world the effect landed before the revocation — legal. In the other it landed after — a violation. Same evidence, both possible. The engine must hold both worlds open, name exactly what evidence would tell them apart, and say clearly what can safely continue in the meantime: look at history, investigate, keep unrelated work going — but no new certifications on the unresolved proof, no blind retries that could double-execute, no lessons promoted claiming a cause we haven't established. When new evidence arrives, the possibilities narrow — and they can narrow in either direction. The decisive test is brutal and simple: show the engine two worlds with identical evidence and demand the same answer for both. If it convicts one and clears the other, it's cheating — reading the answer key, not the evidence.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This makes uncertainty a first-class citizen with calculus: the possible-histories model, May/MustViolate, evidence-monotonic refinement, and the twin-worlds honesty test. The permanent contributions: the three-way conclusion is now four (with the inconsistent-observations case), the unresolved-operation representation (missing receipt ⇒ UNRESOLVED, never fabricated), the operational table for what continues during ambiguity, and the two-layer model check (concrete executions × observable histories) that detects answer-key leakage. Every future system reasoning about incomplete histories inherits this: preserve the set, name the missing evidence, narrow monotonically, never manufacture certainty.

machine_view.spec_only: Framework ratified; ambiguity-qualification extension of the in-build revocation-linearization spec. Bounded verification candidate; not for main.

intelligence.measurement_contract: RFD-AMB-001: two controlled executions (legal and violating) with identical visible observations and withheld effect evidence; verifier establishes both worlds compatible; worker returns AMBIGUOUS_BOTH_POSSIBLE (not PASS, not a fault attribution); staged trusted-evidence release narrows correctly to legal or violating; evidence removal restores ambiguity; independent unaffected claims retain qualifications; a cold successor reconstructs the uncertainty from the record alone. Ten adversarial controls A1–A10 all green. The twin-worlds property D(Observe(h1))=D(Observe(h2)) holds for the diagnosis engine. Completion coverage always declared (exhaustive vs bounded vs sampled).

naya_view.directive: Model histories as sets of possible worlds, never single invented timelines. Compute MayViolate and MustViolate separately; check H(O) is nonempty before universal claims. Preserve partial orders — assert Commit(R)≺Commit(A) only on trusted evidence. Narrow possibilities monotonically as admissible evidence arrives; flag contradictions instead of discarding them. During ambiguity, withhold certification and dependent consequential use while permitting inspection, reconciliation, and unrelated authorized work. Operate the diagnosis engine only on the observable projection; test it with twin worlds to prove no answer-key leakage.

simple_view.meaning: When the evidence can't decide, hold both worlds open, name what's missing, and never invent certainty — then prove the engine can't tell the worlds apart without the evidence.

intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor inherits rigorous uncertainty: possible histories with named missing evidence, monotonic narrowing, and the discipline to say 'we don't know' — never manufacturing certainty from missing receipts.
intelligence.uncertainty: Framework ratified; spec refinement not yet built. Main at 0fb380c (healed); the installation-token-attributed CI failures remain a reported diagnosis, not independent proof.
